Automatic transmission fluid: drain and refill, 2005 Accord EX-L 2.4 L, 5-speed automatic

Sourced Sourced (OM pp.219–221, Chilton)

Honda's schedule
  • Automatic transmission fluid: first at 60,000 mi or 3 yr, then every 30,000 mi or 2 yr (OM p.203 severe)

Sources: Honda owner's manual (OM) "Transmission Fluid", pp.219–221 (read 2026-11-10); capacities OM p.274; Chilton A/T Fluid Replacement and A/T Fluid Level Check, applicability "2003–04 Accord V6 A/T and 2005–07 Accord" (engine not split), report E in sources/chilton-report-A-I-2026-10-27.md; numbers copied in specs.md. Difficulty: easy–moderate (an oil change with a different plug and a funnel in a dipstick tube). Time: ~45–60 min per round (estimate, not from a manual). Undrivable? Only between pulling the plug and finishing the refill (~30 min), as long as the fluid and a washer are bought first.

Why it matters on this car

The automatic is the part most likely to end this car (plans/long-term-ownership.md), the fluid has no service record (maintenance.md), and the 60 mph shake (open issue 3) has a light-throttle shudder pattern in NHTSA complaints that fresh fluid sometimes helps (COMMUNITY). Severe-schedule interval: 60,000 mi or 3 yr, then every 30,000 mi or 2 yr (VERIFIED: OM p.203).

Safety

Steps

Backyard method (COMMUNITY)

Gotchas

  • No pan or gasket in this job. The OM (pp.219–220) and Chilton's A/T Fluid Replacement use only the drain plug and the dipstick tube.
  • External ATF filter: probably exists, not on Honda's schedule. Owner sees a filter under the under-hood fuse box (2026-11-15, no photo yet). Honda catalog (HondaPartsNow category listing, 2026-11-15) shows 25430-PLR-003 "Filter (ATf)" for 2003–2011 Accord trims incl. DX/VP/PZEV (4-cylinder only) with KA/KL 5AT; forums call it an inline filter on a cooler line (COMMUNITY). 25450-RAY-003 is V6 only (HondaPartsNow fitment). The OM maintenance schedule (pp.202–203) has no ATF filter item, and Chilton's only filter article is Hybrid-only (report E, G27): no 4-cyl procedure or torque pulled yet. Don't replace it until a photo confirms what it is, the part is confirmed by VIN, and the Chilton 4-cyl steps are pulled. AutoZone's "complete the job" add-ons for this car (Duralast filter kit TF534, Fel-Pro pan gasket 2304, Lubegard Shudder Fixx; seen 2026-11-14) are not part of Honda's procedure: skip them (TF534 comes with a pan gasket; this transmission has no pan). Additives also break the Honda-fluid rule and would muddy the 60 mph shake test.
  • "Don't change old fluid on a car with no history" (heard at O'Reilly, 2026-11-15). No Honda source says this. Honda's schedule says drain and refill (OM p.220, no exception for missed services), and Honda bulletins for other models fix judder by replacing worn fluid with drain-and-refills (16-060). The warning mostly comes from pressure-machine flushes and from transmissions that were already failing before the change (COMMUNITY/UNVERIFIED). Honda's drain-and-refill is the gentlest way: no pressure, ~43% swapped per round. If the fluid is burnt or the magnet has chunks, the transmission was already worn; the change doesn't cause that, but it won't fix it either.
  • Price check (2026-11-14): AutoZone MaxLife Multi-Vehicle 1 gal $45.99 = ~$11.50/qt, more than Honda DW-1 at $10.75/qt (next-steps.md). One gallon covers one round only.
  • One round replaces only part of the fluid: about 3.0 of 6.9 qt (OM p.274), ~43%. Estimated new-fluid share, assuming the old and new mix fully: 1 round ~43%, 2 ~68%, 3 ~82%, 4 ~90% (Claude's arithmetic from the OM numbers, not a Honda figure). The manual's routine service is one round; the 4-round flush is its "thorough" option (OM p.220).
  • Honda bulletin list on NHTSA includes A89-022 "Using the ATF DW-1 Cooler Cleaner" (Chilton bulletin list item 24): a shop item tied to transmission replacement, not this job. Not read in full.
  • If the fluid comes out burnt-smelling and dark brown with grit, still do the change, but log it: it changes the walk-away math for this car (plans/long-term-ownership.md).

After the job

What I couldn't verify

  • DW-1 replacing Z1 and the drain washer number: Honda parts counter, free, with the VIN.
  • Exact drain plug location photo (owner: passenger side, 3/8-in drive).
  • Jack stand points: Chilton (library) → "Jacking" section; or the OM p.248 jack points are the safe lift points, stands go next to them on the pinch weld (COMMUNITY, UNVERIFIED).
  • "Short distance" between rounds: the manual gives no number.

Brake fluid exchange and coolant change: 2005 Accord EX-L 2.4 L AT

Sourced Brake: sourced; coolant DIY steps from a V6 article (labeled)

Honda's schedule
  • Brake fluid: every 3 yr (OM p.203)
  • Engine coolant: first at 120,000 mi or 10 yr, then every 60,000 mi or 5 yr (OM p.203)

Both are overdue (no record, maintenance.md). Recommended: have a shop do both (plans/2026-11-catch-up-maintenance.md): a brake bleed done wrong leaves air in the brakes, and coolant needs the air bled out and the old coolant disposed of. This file is so you can order the job correctly, check the shop's work, or do it yourself if you choose.

Sources: OM pp.203, 217–218, 223, 257, 274; Chilton bleed order (report B, specs.md); Chilton coolant bleed summary is from the V6 article (sources/chilton-2026-10-23.md C03), labeled below.

---

Part 1. Brake fluid (every 3 years regardless of miles, OM p.203)

ItemValueSource
FluidHonda Heavy Duty Brake Fluid DOT 3; DOT 3 or DOT 4 from a sealed container only as a temporary replacement; never DOT 5VERIFIED: OM p.223
Bleed orderFront left → front right → rear right → rear leftChilton "Accord and Prelude shown" figure (report B, G16): generic figure, specs.md
ABS unitNo scan-tool bleed unless the ABS modulator was openedChilton report (chilton-checklist.md 22)
Bleeder screw torqueNot found. Snug only; don't use a number from memory—
How much fluidNot found (chilton-checklist.md 23). Buy 2 × 12 oz bottles (COMMUNITY, typical for a car this size)—

What to ask the shop for: "Brake fluid exchange with Honda Heavy Duty DOT 3, bled at all four wheels until clean fluid comes out, and a full brake inspection. Please tell me the front pad thickness and rotor thickness, and whether the rear brakes are disc or drum." Time at a shop: ~1 h. Undrivable only while it's there.

DIY two-person method (if you choose it)

Tools: 8 mm or 10 mm wrench for the bleeders (size not confirmed: check before buying), clear hose that fits the bleeder snugly, bottle, helper, jack + stands, turkey baster. Time ~1.5 h first time (estimate). The car is undrivable until done.

Backyard tool (COMMUNITY): a one-person check-valve bleeder bottle (~$10–20) or a hand vacuum pump (often free as a parts-store loaner). Why it works: the check valve or vacuum stops air being sucked back in at the bleeder when the pedal comes up, so one person can do it. Still check pedal feel before driving.

Honda bulletin A07-045 "Brake Pedal Is Low and Feels Soft" exists for this model (tsbs.md, Chilton list): not read in full. If the pedal is soft after a correct bleed, ask the shop about it.

---

Part 2. Coolant (120,000 mi or 10 yr, then every 60,000 mi or 5 yr; OM p.203)

ItemValueSource
CoolantHonda All Season Antifreeze/Coolant Type 2, premixed 50/50. Never straight antifreeze, never plain water (except to get home). No additives or rust inhibitorsVERIFIED: OM pp.217–218
Change amount (automatic)1.32 US gal (5.0 L) incl. reserve tankVERIFIED: OM p.274; Chilton 5.3 qt agrees
Total1.88 US gal (7.1 L)VERIFIED: OM p.274
Honda part (premixed)OL999-9001 (Chilton V6 article): confirm at the counterparts.md
Radiator cap pressure, thermostat temperatureNot found (chilton-checklist.md 40)—

Before paying anyone: look at the reserve tank cold (level, colour). Honda Type 2 is blue (COMMUNITY: well known; the bottle shows it). Rusty brown, oily, or crusty = do it soon and ask the shop to pressure-test for leaks. Clean blue at the right level = it can wait a month or two.

What to ask the shop for: "Drain and refill with Honda Type 2 premixed coolant, air bled out, no flush chemicals." Time ~1 h; undrivable while there.

DIY outline (steps from Chilton's V6 article, C03: UNVERIFIED for the 2.4 L)

Engine cold (OM p.217 warning). Heater set to max hot. Drain at the radiator drain plug into a pan; refill the radiator to the base of the filler neck and the reserve tank to MAX; run with the cap off/loose until the fan cycles at least twice, topping up as bubbles come out; cap on, reserve to MAX; check for leaks; recheck the level cold next morning. Old coolant is toxic and sweet-tasting to animals: sealed jug to a parts store or recycler.

Backyard tool (COMMUNITY): a spill-free funnel kit (~$20–35, or a parts-store loaner) that clamps to the radiator neck. Why it works: the funnel sits higher than the engine, so trapped air rises out through it instead of staying in the head and causing a false overheat.

---

After either job

log.md with the odometer, product and amount; update the row in maintenance.md (brake fluid next due in 3 years; coolant 60,000 mi or 5 yr).

What I couldn't verify

  • Bleeder wrench size and bleeder torque: Chilton (library) or look at the bleeder.
  • Brake flush fluid amount: Chilton checklist 23.
  • 2.4 L coolant drain/bleed steps, radiator cap pressure, thermostat temperature: Chilton 2006–07 Accord 2.4 L "Coolant Replacement" (library).
  • Whether the rear brakes are disc or drum on this EX: look through the rear wheel (free).

Tire rotation: 2005 Accord EX-L sedan

Sourced Sourced (OM p.239, p.250)

Honda's schedule
  • Tire rotation: every 10,000 mi (OM p.203 severe)

Sources: OM p.239 (rotation pattern and interval), p.250 (lug torque, crisscross), p.238 (balance, wheel weights), p.248 (jack points). Read 2026-11-10. Difficulty: easy with two jack stands. Time: ~45 min DIY (estimate); free or cheap at a tire shop, often bundled with a balance. Car is undrivable only while it's up.

On this car right now: wait. Don't rotate until open issue 11 (ditch damage, bead leak) and open issue 3 (60 mph shake) are checked, and chalk each tire's old position first (LF, RF, LR, RR) so a wobble that moves with a wheel shows which one it is (maintenance.md).

Pattern (VERIFIED: OM p.239)

  • Non-directional tires: fronts go straight back (same side); rears cross to the front (left rear → right front, right rear → left front).
  • Directional tires (arrow on the sidewall): front-to-back only, same side.
  • Every 10,000 mi (4-cylinder).

Steps

Backyard notes (COMMUNITY)

log.md (date, odometer, old → new positions, tread depth if measured); maintenance.md tire rotation row. A vibration that's new after rotating = balance, or the wheel that moved (OM p.238: "have the tires rebalanced"; aluminum wheels take genuine Honda wheel weights).

Front brake pads and rotors: 2005 Accord EX-L 2.4 L

Sourced Sourced (Chilton F03 + spec table; two TENTATIVE values flagged)

Sources: Chilton Brakes > Front Disc Brakes > Pads / Rotor R&I (pack F03; front figure captioned V6, text not engine-specific); Chilton Brake Specifications table, 2005 Accord row (report B), and the 2026-10-23 pull (specs.md); lug torque OM p.250. Difficulty: moderate. Time: ~1.5–2 h for both front corners, first time (estimate). Undrivable from the first caliper bolt until the pedal is firm again: start in the morning on a day off, parts in hand.

Battery, charging and parasitic draw tests: 2005 Accord EX-L 2.4 L

Sourced Partly sourced (charging limits from a TSX article, labeled)

For open issues 2 (P0685), 6 (past drains) and 9 (USB drops). Cheap-first: the parts-store tests are free; the draw test needs only a multimeter (owner bought one, 2026-11-05).

Sources: battery rating OM p.275; battery care OM pp.242–243; jump OM pp.253–255; charging fault limits are from Chilton's Acura TSX article (same K24 family, not confirmed for this car, specs.md). Steps without a source: standard practice, labeled. Car stays drivable throughout.

1. Free tests at a chain parts store (~15 min)

Ask for a battery load/conductance test and a charging system test. Bring the car with the engine cold-ish so they can test cranking. Write the printout numbers into log.md. Battery: EverStart Maxx, made May 2025, rated 12 V 38 AH/5 HR minimum (OM p.275), under warranty (owner).

2. Quick voltage checks with the multimeter (~10 min)

ConditionReadingWhat it meansSource
Engine off, sat 2+ h~12.6 V full; ~12.2 V about half; under 12.0 V dischargedBattery stateCOMMUNITY (general lead-acid table)
Engine running, 2,000 rpm, lights offFault if over 15.1 V or under 13.5 VChargingChilton TSX article (UNVERIFIED for this car)
Engine running, flick high beams / rear defrostShould stay in range; a big drop = weak alternator or bad connectionLoadCOMMUNITY
Voltage drop: meter from battery − post to engine block while crankingOver ~0.3 V = bad ground (COMMUNITY rule of thumb)Ground pathCOMMUNITY
Same, battery + post to alternator output stud, engine running with loads onOver ~0.3 V = bad positive cable/connectionFeed pathCOMMUNITY

Measure on the posts, then on the clamps: a difference between the two = the clamp contact is bad (the loose terminal found 2026-10-31).

3. Parasitic draw test (~1 h, mostly waiting)

Needs the meter's 10 A jack. The car must be "asleep".

Safety: don't crank the engine or switch on headlights with the meter in series: it will blow the meter's fuse. Battery gas is explosive: no sparks near it (OM p.243).

4. If the battery tests bad

Warranty swap at the store. Before installing the new one: clean both clamps (baking soda and water, OM p.242), check the group size label (51R is unverified, parts.md). Disconnect negative first, reconnect it last (OM p.242). Radio code: owner has it. After a disconnect the readiness monitors take 3+ days to reset (OM p.260); the power window auto function may need a reset (Chilton checklist 51).

What I couldn't verify

  • Honda's charging voltage spec and max parasitic draw for the 2005 2.4 L: Chilton (library) checklist 46–47; bulletin A10-054 also covers charging diagnosis.
  • Battery group size: label on the battery.

Valve clearance: inspect and adjust. 2005 Accord EX-L 2.4 L K24A4

Draft: not fully sourced DRAFT; exhaust spec in conflict, shop recommended

Honda's schedule
  • Valve clearance: inspect: first at 110,000 mi (OM p.203 (then only if noisy))

DRAFT, shop job recommended. The exhaust spec is still in conflict (specs.md), and no 2.4 L procedure has been pulled. No adjustment until the spec is settled.

Interval: inspect at 110,000 mi, otherwise adjust only if noisy (VERIFIED: OM pp.202–203). Car is at ~139k with no record: due.

Specs (both shown; which ranks higher in specs.md)

SourceIntakeExhaustNote
Chilton tune-up table, 2005 2.4 K24A4 row0.008–0.010 in0.011–0.013 inRead as "cold" in one pull, no cold label in the other
Chilton Acura TSX article0.21–0.25 mm (0.008–0.010 in)0.25–0.29 mm (0.010–0.011 in)Head below 100 °F
Locknut torqueTSX: intake 15 lbf·ft (20 N·m), exhaust 10 lbf·ft (14 N·m)TSX only, not confirmed for this engine

Intake agrees. Exhaust differs by ~0.002 in at the top of the range: settle it from a 2006–07 Accord 2.4 L article (prompts/muse-chilton-pull-3.md S01) or a Honda dealer before adjusting.

What to ask a shop

"Valve clearance inspection, cold engine, adjust only out-of-spec valves to Honda's 2.4 L K24A4 spec, new valve cover gasket and spark plug tube seals, tell me which valves were out and by how much." Ask which spec they used and write it here. Time at a shop: a few hours (estimate); off the road for the day.

Why it matters (COMMUNITY reasoning, UNVERIFIED for this engine)

Exhaust valves on high-mileage engines tend to tighten, not loosen; a tight valve doesn't tick, it quietly stops sealing fully and can burn. So "adjust only if noisy" doesn't catch the risky case. That's why an inspection past 110k is worth paying for.

DIY outline (only after the spec is settled)

Cold engine (TSX article: head under 100 °F). Valve cover off (coils out first, accord-2005-spark-plugs.md). Rotate the crank to each cylinder's TDC on compression (crank pulley bolt, clockwise). Feeler gauge between rocker and valve tip; adjust with the locknut and screw; torque the locknut. New gasket and tube seals; cover bolts to the 2.4 L torque and sequence (not found yet, checklist 32).

Still needed

Exhaust spec settled; valve cover bolt torque and sequence; locknut torques for the 2.4 L.

Winter prep: 2005 Accord EX-L 2.4 L AT (only car, Washington winters)

Sourced Sourced (OM pp.216–253)

Sources: OM pp.216–217 (washer fluid, coolant), p.225 (hood latch), pp.237–241 (tires, snow tires, chains), pp.242–243 (battery), p.253 (frozen battery), p.199 (severe schedule conditions). Read 2026-11-10. Items without an OM page are labeled. Time: ~1 h of checks, plus whatever they turn up. Car stays drivable.

#CheckWhat to doSource
1CoolantHonda Type 2 premixed 50/50 gives freeze protection without mixing; never top up with plain water in winter. Overdue for a change (maintenance.md): look at it cold; murky or low → do the change before a hard freezeOM p.217; change: procedures/accord-2005-brake-fluid-coolant.md
2Washer fluidWinter-rated commercial washer fluid only. No engine antifreeze (damages paint), no vinegar/water (damages the pump). Run summer fluid low first so it doesn't diluteOM p.216
3BatteryFree load test at a parts store before the first cold snap (cold cuts cranking power; COMMUNITY, general). Terminals clean and tight (open issue 2). Never jump a frozen battery (slushy/frozen electrolyte can burst)OM pp.242, 253
4TiresCheck pressures more often: cold air lowers the reading (COMMUNITY: roughly 1 psi per 10 °F). Set to 32/30 cold (OM p.237). Tread: replace at 3+ wear bars (OM p.238). The left front bead leak (open issue 11) must be fixed before winterOM pp.236–238
5Snow tires (if bought)Radial, same size and load range as the originals (P205/60R16 91V), on all four wheels. Their dry-road grip can be lower; ask the dealer about speed ratingOM p.240
6Chains (EX)Cable type only: SCC Radial Chain CH2311T or SCC SC Cable SC1030 (limited clearance on this car). Front tires only, as tight as possible, slow; stop if they hit the body. Never on the compact spareOM pp.241, 246
7WipersReplace if streaking (blades are from 2026-09). Lift the arms off the glass in an ice storm; don't open the hood with them raisedOM pp.234–235
8Hood latchClean and grease the latch pivots (sticks in freezing rain)OM p.225
9LightsAll working (dark commutes): procedures/accord-2005-routine-checks.md. Aim if they light the trees, not the roadOM pp.201, 226
10RustRinse the underbody every couple of weeks when roads are de-iced. De-iced roads also put the car on the severe maintenance scheduleplans/long-term-ownership.md; OM p.199
11Emergency kitJumper cables or a jump pack, flashlight, tire inflator, gloves, blanket, ice scraper, the spare at 60 psiCOMMUNITY; spare pressure OM p.246
12Door sealsA silicone spray on the door and trunk seals keeps them from freezing shutOM p.244 (storage tips)

Driving notes for this car this winter: ABS is not working until the bearing is replaced (open issue 4): in a skid, braking can lock the front tires, and locked front tires don't steer (UNVERIFIED reasoning: general vehicle dynamics; it's how the ditch slide happened). Leave more room, brake earlier and gently, and get item 3 of next-steps.md done first.

Exterior bulbs: 2005 Accord EX-L sedan, 2.4 L

Sourced Sourced (OM pp.226–232)

Sources: Honda owner's manual (OM) "Lights", pp.226–232 (page images read 2026-11-10); bulb ratings OM p.275 (specs.md). Difficulty: easy. Time: 5–20 min per bulb (estimate). Car stays drivable. Tools: flat screwdriver (fender clips), nothing else per the manual.

Before you start

High beam (OM pp.227–228)

Low beam (through the wheel well) (OM pp.228–229)

Front side marker / turn signal / parking (OM pp.229–230)

Same wheel-well access as the low beam (steer, two clips, pull the liner back). Socket 1/4 turn counterclockwise out of the headlight assembly. Bulb: push in and turn counterclockwise. New bulb, socket back in clockwise, test, liner and clips back.

Rear bulbs in the fenders (OM p.230)

Trunk open → pull the light assembly cover off by its outside edge → socket 1/4 turn counterclockwise → bulb pulls straight out → new bulb pushed straight in until it bottoms → socket back clockwise → test → cover back.

Rear bulbs in the trunk lid (OM p.231)

Trunk open. (The manual's trim-clip removal step is marked for the 6-cylinder only.) Bend back the corner of the trunk-lid trim to expose the sockets → socket 1/4 turn counterclockwise → bulb pulls straight out → new bulb in, socket back → test → trim back, clips pressed in. A trim clip that breaks: a dealer or parts store sells them cheap; don't glue.

High-mount brake light (OM p.232)

Trunk open; under the rear shelf, socket 1/4 turn counterclockwise → bulb pulls straight out → new bulb, socket back.

Interior bulbs

Not covered by the manual's steps. Dome bulb confirmed as a 31 mm festoon, 8 W (owner, 2026-10-26, parts.md); map lights and trunk bulb not yet read. The middle courtesy light dims with the instrument-panel brightness, so an LED there may flicker (OM p.101, specs.md).

After

log.md: which bulb, brand/number, date, odometer.

Roadside: flat tire, jump start, overheating, warning lights, towing (2005 Accord EX-L 2.4 L AT)

Sourced Sourced (OM pp.245–264)

Sources: Honda owner's manual (OM) "Taking Care of the Unexpected", pp.245–264 (page images read 2026-11-10). Every step below is from those pages unless labeled otherwise. It's the only car: keep the spare aired up (60 psi, OM p.246), jumper cables or a jump pack, and a flashlight in it.

Flat tire (OM pp.246–251)

Time: ~20–30 min (estimate). Leaves the car drivable on the spare: 50 mph max (OM p.246), harsher ride, less grip; get the real tire fixed or replaced soon.

COMMUNITY tip: carry a cheap 1/2-in breaker bar + 19 mm or 21 mm socket (check your lug size before buying: not in the manual) and a 12 V tire inflator. Why: the factory wrench is short, and a slow leak (like the bead leak in open issue 11) is often fixable by airing up and driving to a tire shop instead of changing the wheel at all.

Plugging a tire: only a tread puncture. Never a sidewall, bead or shoulder leak (that's a dismount-and-inspect job). Honda's bulletin A06-082 "Tubeless Tire Repair Information" exists (Chilton bulletin list); not read in full.

Engine won't start (OM pp.251–252)

What you hearCheckThen
Nothing, clicks, or slow crankIn P or N? Key ON, headlights on: very dim or dead = batteryClean/tighten battery terminals (OM p.242), then jump start
Headlights fine but dim/go out when crankingBattery discharged or corroded connectionsTerminals, then jump
Headlights don't dim at all, starter silentFuses (OM pp.265–269)If fuses OK: starter/ignition circuit, tow
Starter spins normally, engine won't runRight starting method (OM p.175)? Immobilizer light blinking rapidly = key not recognised (OM p.77)? Fuel?Fuses (fuel pump: interior #19 IG Fuel Pump 15 A). Still nothing: tow

Car-specific: recall 07V097000 (fuel pump relay) and 05V132000 (fuse box terminal) were both no-start/stall causes on this model. NHTSA shows neither open on this VIN (profile.md). Open issue 2 (P0685, main relay circuit) is the same family of fault.

Jump start (OM pp.253–255)

Push-starting an automatic is impossible (OM p.253).

Overheating (OM pp.256–257)

Never open the radiator cap hot (OM pp.217, 257). Driving at red damages the engine.

Warning lights while driving

Wheel alignment (DIY string method): 2005 Accord EX sedan, 2.4 L, automatic

Draft: not fully sourced DRAFT

Status: DRAFT. Not done on this car yet, and the steps are not checked against the factory service manual. Targets are from the owner's manual; tolerances, torque specs and wrench sizes are not. Before the first real use, read the FSM wheel alignment section in Chilton Library (free with a library card) and fill in the "Still needed" list at the end.

Sources: owner's manual p.275 (targets, via specs.md) · OM p.250 (lug nuts) · OM p.276 (tire pressure) · DIY method write-ups and DriveAccord threads (COMMUNITY, linked inline) Difficulty: moderate · Time: ~3–4 h the first time, mostly setup (estimate, not sourced); ~1–1.5 h once you've done it

What DIY can and can't do on this car

AngleAdjustable from the factory?DIY?
Front toeYes, at the tie rodsYes. This is the one that matters most for tire wear and the one you'll adjust most often
Rear toeYes, cam (eccentric) bolts on the rear toe arms. COMMUNITY: DriveAccord, rear toe arm threadYes, if the cam bolts aren't seized
Thrust angleFollows from rear toeYes: make the two rear wheels' toe equal
Front camberNo. COMMUNITY: DriveAccord, "Is camber adjustable on these cars? No". Correcting it needs an aftermarket adjustable upper arm or similarMeasure only. A reading off spec or different side to side points to a bent or worn part
Front casterNo. COMMUNITY: DriveAccord, front caster threadMeasure only (optional, fiddly)
Rear camberSmall range at most. COMMUNITY reports differ; adjustable rear arms exist for moreMeasure only

Honest call: for toe, a careful string setup is the standard home method. For camber/caster diagnosis after a crash, a curb strike or hammering on the knuckle, a shop's printout is more trustworthy than a phone-sized angle gauge. One paid printout also documents the car for resale.

Aftermarket camber arms are bolt-on and reversible (owner's rules allow that), but they replace OEM parts: keep the originals if you ever fit them.

When to align

Targets

From specs.md (VERIFIED: OM p.275):

FrontRear
Toe-in0.00 in (0.0 mm)0.08 in (2.0 mm)
Camber0°1° (sign not printed; very likely negative, UNVERIFIED)
Caster3°15′—

Not in the owner's manual (need the FSM): the tolerance (± range) on each value, whether the toe figures are total (both wheels added) or per wheel, the diameter the toe is measured at, and the vehicle condition (load, fuel) for measuring.

What that means in practice:

  • Front toe target is zero, so it reads the same at any diameter and whether total or per wheel. Set the front to zero, equal side to side.
  • Rear toe is tiny. If 2.0 mm is total toe measured at the tire tread (~652 mm for a P205/60R16: 406 mm wheel + 2 × 123 mm sidewall), then across ~430 mm of rim lip it's about 1.3 mm total, ~0.7 mm per wheel. That's about the limit of reading a tape. So for the rear, aim for: slight toe-in, never toe-out, and both sides equal. To convert any linear toe to your measuring span: spec × (your span ÷ spec diameter).

Tools and parts

Safety

Steps

Prep (~30 min)

Set up the strings (~45 min the first time)

Measure toe (~20 min)

Adjust front toe (~30–45 min)

Rear toe (only if it's off; ~30–60 min)

Camber check (~15 min)

Caster (optional)

Finish

Gotchas

  • COMMUNITY: reading a tape to 1 mm reliably is hard, and a string a hair off parallel shows up as fake toe. Recheck string parallel/centering before believing a reading (Garage Journal thread).
  • COMMUNITY: measure on the wheel, not the tire (The Mustang Source, DIY toe).
  • Front toe moves when the car sits up or down: always settle the car before measuring (general practice).
  • Doesn't leave the car undrivable if you only touch toe and mark start positions, except a seized rear cam bolt or a stripped tie rod thread. Do the first one on a day off.

Still needed from the FSM (Chilton Library, free with a library card)

  • Toe, camber, caster tolerances.
  • Whether toe is total or per wheel, and at what diameter.
  • Rear camber sign (expected −1°).
  • Vehicle condition for measuring (load, fuel, spare).
  • Torque: outer tie rod jam nut, rear toe arm (cam bolt) nut.
  • Wrench sizes for both.
  • Honda's own alignment procedure, to replace or confirm steps 15–25.
